inputs.original_text: It's absolutely heartbreaking to learn the US is pulling out of the Paris Agreement for the second time under the Donald Trump administration, especially since China and the United States played a key role in building this global framework. This move just deepens the entrenched systemic inequalities that let powerful nations and their corporate backers escape accountability for the climate crisis they've driven through centuries of exploitation and unchecked greed. Marginalized communities will bear the worst of it, as they already are, relying on international efforts to endure the disasters created by these profit-first systems. We need to fight for structural reforms that actually safeguard the vulnerable instead of defending these broken institutions.
inputs.modified_text: The Donald Trump administration's decision to have the US pull out of the Paris Agreement for the second time is devastating. It represents a further entrenchment of systemic inequalities that permit powerful nations and corporate interests to dodge responsibility for the climate crisis resulting from centuries of exploitation and greed. It's the marginalized communities that will face the harshest consequences, depending on international frameworks to cope with the disasters stemming from profit-driven systems. Rather than defending these broken institutions, we must pursue structural reforms to protect the vulnerable.
